text:
Mikael Granlund is 34, on his sixth NHL team, and scoring like he did a decade ago. He has 26 points in 21 games for Anaheim, including 12 on the power play, and 18 in his last ten, well above the 10.5 we'd expect at his 21 minutes a night.

Our read is that it's partly real. Anaheim's chances with him on the ice are up a little (17.7 on-ice expected goals in that stretch against 15.4 usual). But finishing is doing most of the work: the Ducks have scored 10.1 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there, and he's shooting 20% against a talent range near 15%.

The worry is at even strength, where Anaheim gets only 41% of the expected goals (chance quality) when he plays 5v5. That's the number that usually wins out over a season. The veteran craft is real, too: All Three Zones tracking had 62% of his zone exits leaving with possession. Enjoy the run, and watch whether the 5v5 share climbs or the points fall to meet it.
headline: Granlund's renaissance comes with a catch
